newsitem.title: USA: Hartford to give extra $2mln to troubled schools.
newsitem.headline: Hartford to give extra $2mln to troubled schools.

text.p: The city of Hartford will contribute an additional $2 million to the troubled school system's current budget, city officials said on Monday.
The amount is some $200,000 more than requested by the Hartford Board of Education, the City Council said in a statement.
The school system gets three-quarters of its $174 million operating budget from state taxpayers.
The additional funds are earmarked for classroom supplies, including 500 computers and 125 printers, the City Council said.
Textbooks and library supplies will also be included. Delivery could be as soon as next week, the City Council said.
Connecticut, last month, approved a dramatic state takeover of Hartford's crisis-torn school system, replacing the board of education with a state-appointed panel.
The school system has been plagued by chronic management problems and the lowest test scores in the state.
Other problems include crumbling buildings, financial mismangement and intense poverty.
